Nobody else ordered on that day. Dora Novak placed one order, a desk mat for €19.00 on 2026-07-21, and no other customer has an order dated 2026-07-21.

To make sure a different date format wasn't hiding a match, I looked through all 8 orders in the database. All the dates are in the same format, and the closest ones to Dora's are:
- Ana Costa, 2026-08-14 (desk lamp)
- Ben Okafor, 2026-08-19 (mouse)

calls.sql:
SELECT d.ordered_on AS dora_date, c.name, o.item, o.total_eur, o.ordered_on
FROM customers dc JOIN orders d ON d.customer_id = dc.id
JOIN orders o ON date(o.ordered_on) = date(d.ordered_on) AND o.customer_id <> dc.id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE dc.name = 'Dora Novak'
ORDER BY d.ordered_on, c.name
SELECT c.id, c.name, o.* FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id WHERE c.name LIKE '%Dora%' OR c.name LIKE '%Novak%'
SELECT o.*, c.name FROM orders o LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id=o.customer_id ORDER BY o.id
